info.title: india-subscriptions HTTP API
info.description: One API over subscriptions and payments on Indian payment gateways (Razorpay, Cashfree, PayU, PhonePe, Paytm) and app stores (Apple App Store, Google Play), with a gateway router and purchase sessions. Amounts are integer paise and instants are ISO-8601 strings.

post.summary: Verify, apply and normalise a forwarded webhook
post.description: For apps that receive the gateway webhook themselves: forward the exact raw body and the headers here. The signature is verified, each event is applied to the billing scheduler (so a mandate that was authorised, paused or cancelled at the gateway is reflected in billing), and the events are returned normalised. Forwarding the same webhook twice is safe. A bad signature answers 401 and changes nothing.

Provider.description: A supported provider: a payment gateway or an app store.

Currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Only INR is supported.

SubscriptionStatus.description: Normalised subscription lifecycle. Each gateway's own status is preserved verbatim in `providerStatus`. `cancelled`, `completed`, `expired` and `failed` are terminal.

ChargeStatus.description: Normalised status of a charge (one debit).

ChargeKind.description: `authorization` is the small verification debit taken when the mandate is set up, `recurring` is a debit for a billing cycle, `upfront` is a one-off amount such as a setup fee or add-on.

PaymentMethod.description: `upi` is a UPI Autopay mandate, `card` a card standing instruction, `enach` an eNACH e-mandate on a bank account, `physical_nach` a paper NACH mandate. `netbanking` and `wallet` apply to one-time payments only.

SchedulingMode.description: Who decides when each recurring debit happens: `gateway` raises every charge on the plan's schedule, `merchant` means the merchant (this library's scheduler) raises each charge.

EventType.description: Normalised webhook / lifecycle event. `unknown` is a verified event this library does not normalise; inspect `raw`.

Environment.description: `test` is the gateway sandbox, `live` is real money.

CancelMode.description: `immediately` stops now with no further charges; `at_period_end` keeps the current paid period, then stops.

ChangeTiming.description: When a subscription change takes effect: `immediately`, or `at_period_end` (the next cycle boundary).

platforms.description: The platforms the product is sold on. Omit for all of them.

paymentMethods.description: Restrict gateway purchases of the product to these payment methods. Only gateways that offer one of them are chosen, and the gateway is told to offer only these. Omit to allow every method the gateway supports.

appStore.description: The product in App Store Connect. Required to sell on iOS.

googlePlay.description: The product in Play Console. Required to sell on Android when the policy is `store` or `user_choice`.

plan.description: Extra plan fields for gateway subscriptions, such as `maxAmount`.

Product.description: A product you sell, with its price and where it lives in each store.

android.description: Android: `store` (Google Play only), `user_choice` (Google Play with its choice screen offering a gateway, reported to Google) or `gateways` (apps distributed outside Google Play).

PlatformPolicy.description: Where purchases on each platform may be taken.

channel.description: `store` for an app store, `gateway` for a payment gateway.

provider.description: The provider that holds the purchase.

checkout.description: What the browser or device must do to pay.

handle.description: The id the provider returned when the purchase was created: the id to expect back from the checkout. For a store it is the account token.

routing.description: Why this gateway was chosen. Present on gateway options.

hostedUrl.description: A page that performs this option's checkout step, for a client that cannot run the browser helper (the Android alternative path opens it in a browser tab). Present on gateway options when the service serves a hosted checkout.

PurchaseOption.description: One way the customer can pay for the session.

provider.description: The gateway that was tried.

outcome.description: Whether the gateway created the order or mandate.

errorCode.description: The error code of a failed attempt.

message.description: The error message of a failed attempt.

PurchaseAttempt.description: One gateway tried while creating the purchase.

id.description: The session id. Unguessable: whoever holds it can complete the session.

platform.description: The platform the customer buys on.

policy.description: The channel policy the session was resolved with: `store`, `user_choice` or `gateways`.

reference.description: Your own id for the purchase: at most 25 characters of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, the tightest limit among the gateways. Retrying a start with the same reference and customer returns the same session.

returnUrl.description: Where the customer is sent when the purchase is done: the `returnUrl` given to `start`.

options.description: How the customer can pay. A `user_choice` session has the Google Play option first and the gateway option once the customer chose the alternative.

attempts.description: Every gateway tried while creating the gateway option, in order.

externalTransactionToken.description: Set when the customer chose the alternative payment on Google's screen.

subscriptionId.description: The provider's subscription id, once the purchase is confirmed.

paymentId.description: The provider's payment id, once the purchase is confirmed.

provider.description: The provider the purchase was confirmed at.

PurchaseSession.description: A purchase in progress or done: where the customer may pay and how it ended.

provider.description: The provider that holds the purchase.

platform.description: The platform the customer bought on.

active.description: True when the item gives access now.

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: True when the subscription ends at the end of the current period.

currentPeriodEnd.description: End of the current paid period, where known.

EntitlementItem.description: One purchase the customer owns or owned.

active.description: True when at least one item gives access now.

items.description: Every purchase of the customer, newest change first, including ended ones.

Entitlements.description: What a customer owns, across app stores and gateways.

platform.description: The platform the customer buys on.

customer.description: The paying customer. `state` is required when the platform policy is `user_choice`, because the purchase is then reported to Google.

customerRef.description: Your id for the customer: entitlements are kept under it.

reference.description: Your own id for the purchase: at most 25 characters of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, the tightest limit among the gateways. Retrying a start with the same reference and customer returns the same session.

returnUrl.description: Where a gateway sends the customer after paying.

StartPurchaseInput.description: Everything needed to start a purchase.

externalTransactionToken.description: The token Google gave the app when the customer chose the alternative on its choice screen.

ChooseAlternativeInput.description: The customer's choice of the alternative payment on Google's screen.

provider.description: The provider the customer paid at.

result.description: What the provider handed back to the browser or device, untouched.

CompletePurchaseInput.description: The result of a checkout, to complete a purchase session with.

limit.description: Most reports to send in this flush. Defaults to 50.

outcome.description: What the flush did with the report. Absent for an overdue report this flush did not try.

attempts.description: Attempts made so far, including this one.

dueBy.description: When Google must have the report.

overdue.description: True when the report was not sent by `dueBy`.

errorCode.description: The error code of a failed attempt.

errorMessage.description: The error message of a failed attempt.

FlushEntry.description: What a flush did with one report.

sent.description: Reports Google accepted in this flush.

retrying.description: Reports whose attempt failed and that stay queued with a backoff.

blocked.description: Reports waiting for an earlier report to be sent.

rejected.description: Reports Google refused as invalid. They are not retried.

skipped.description: Reports left queued because no reporter is configured.

entries.description: One entry per report this flush looked at.

overdue.description: Every queued report past its `dueBy`, whether or not this flush tried it. Page someone when this is not empty.

FlushResult.description: The outcome of sending queued reports to Google.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response.

code.description: What went wrong. Branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Do not branch on it.

provider.description: The gateway involved, where one was.

httpStatus.description: The gateway's HTTP status, when it answered. This is not the status of this response.

providerCode.description: The gateway's own error code, verbatim.

retryable.description: True when repeating the same call later is safe and may succeed.

ErrorDetail.description: The error: a stable code, a message and, for gateway failures, what the gateway said.

ErrorCode.description: A stable error code: one of the library's `ErrorCode`s or one of the service's own (`UNAUTHORIZED`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`). Branch on this, never on the message.

providers.description: The gateways this service is configured with.

received.description: Number of events the gateway's webhook carried.

WebhookReceipt.description: Acknowledgement of a webhook the service verified.

WebhookPayload.description: The gateway's webhook body, exactly as the gateway sent it.

recorded.description: True when the router counted the outcome.

RoutingReceipt.description: Acknowledgement of an outcome the router recorded.

limit.description: Most schedules to process in this run.

TickRequest.description: Options for one run of the billing scheduler.

openapi.description: The OpenAPI version of the document.

OpenApiDocument.description: This API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document.

TickError.description: A failure of one schedule during a tick.

due.description: Schedules the store reported as due.

locked.description: Due schedules skipped because another worker held their lock.

notified.description: Pre-debit notifications accepted by the gateway.

awaiting.description: Cycles left waiting for the gateway's final answer.

halted.description: Schedules halted because a cycle exhausted its attempts.

expired.description: Pending-authorisation schedules cancelled by their timeout.

errors.description: Schedules that failed during this tick; the others are unaffected.

TickResult.description: What one run of the billing scheduler did. A failing schedule shows up in `errors`; the others are unaffected.

LibraryErrorCode.description: Stable error code of this library. Branch on it, never on the message.

EventsDelivery.description: Anything the service POSTs to the events webhook; switch on `kind`.

kind.description: Always `gateway`: tells this delivery from a scheduler one.

provider.description: The gateway whose webhook carried the events.

events.description: The verified, normalised events of one gateway webhook, in the order the gateway sent them. Each has an `id` to de-duplicate on.

GatewayEventsDelivery.description: A delivery of gateway webhook events to the events webhook.

kind.description: Always `scheduler`: tells this delivery from a gateway one.

events.description: Billing scheduler events in the order they happened. Each has an `id` to de-duplicate on.

SchedulerEventsDelivery.description: A delivery of billing scheduler events to the events webhook.

provider.description: The gateway holding the mandate.

subscriptionId.description: The gateway subscription id of the schedule.

scheduleStatus.description: The status of the schedule after the change.

reason.description: Why the schedule changed status, where relevant.

attempt.description: The debit attempt concerned, where relevant.

chargeId.description: The debit id concerned, where relevant.

amount.description: The amount in paise concerned, where relevant.

id.description: Stable id for de-duplication: the same scheduler event always has the same id, so a repeated delivery can be ignored.

SchedulerWebhookEvent.description: A state change of a billing schedule, with a stable id.

SchedulerEventType.description: What happened to a schedule, as reported to the `onEvent` listener.

ScheduleStatus.description: Lifecycle of one scheduled subscription: pending_authorization (nothing is billed yet), active, paused, halted (retries exhausted), cancelled or completed (all cycles collected or the mandate ended).

ScheduleStatusReason.description: Why a schedule is in its current status, for dashboards and audit logs.
